title: A hymn in Kanara
hook: Guru Arjan's hymn of a person with no enemy and no stranger, and how he got there

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raga Kanara, the night raga, and Guru Ram Das's mind turned green by good company. Your line was night. Whose company did you name before sleep? A new week starts now. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-one.

The person at the next table. The driver. A name scrolling past in the comments. Not disliked, exactly; just not counted yet. That's what a stranger is. A hymn of Guru Arjan in Raga Kanara says, in plain English: no one is my enemy, no one is a stranger. It's a big thing for anyone to say, and the second half asks more than the first. The hymn says that whole category has emptied out. And it tells you how. Today: a hymn in Kanara.
screen: `NO ONE IS MY ENEMY.` → `NO ONE IS A STRANGER.` → `AND IT TELLS YOU HOW.`

segments.voice: Here's the hymn, in paraphrase, in its own order. It begins with what went missing: I have forgotten all my jealousy of others, ever since I found the company of the holy. Then the line we started with: no one is my enemy, no one is a stranger; I get along with everyone. Then: whatever God does, I accept as good; this wisdom I received from the holy. And it ends: the One God is present in all, and seeing this, Nanak blossoms. Look at the order, because the hymn is building something. First, jealousy goes. That's the quiet engine of a lot of distance between people, comparing, keeping score. With it gone, enemies are harder to keep. Then strangers go too, because the hymn's last line explains why nobody is foreign anymore: the same One is present in every one of them. And the source of all of it is named twice: the company of the holy. That's yesterday's thread, picked up in the same raga. Guru Ram Das's mind turned green in good company. Here, in Guru Arjan's hymn, that same company empties out jealousy, enemies and strangers. The word for stranger in the hymn is bigana, an outsider, someone who isn't one of yours. The hymn doesn't say strangers stop existing. It says, from where this person stands, there aren't any left. And the closing image is not a rule but a flowering: seeing the One in everyone, Nanak blossoms. Your line: no stranger.
screen: `FIRST, JEALOUSY IS FORGOTTEN.` · `NO ENEMY, NO STRANGER.` · `WHATEVER GOD DOES, ACCEPTED AS GOOD.` · `THE ONE IN ALL; NANAK BLOSSOMS.` · then, large: `NO STRANGER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to one Kanara shabad, and bring one stranger in from the edge. If you can, play this hymn or another shabad sung in Kanara. If not, sit in the quiet. Breathe slowly. Bring to mind someone you passed today without really seeing: a cashier, a neighbor, a face on a screen. Let them stand in front of you for a few breaths. They have a morning, a family, a worry, just as you do. You don't need to feel anything in particular. Just let them stop being background. If you pray, you can hold the hymn's last thought, that the One is present in them too. The bell holds the time.
A hymn in Kanara. Guru Arjan's song of forgetting jealousy in the company of the holy, until no one is an enemy, no one a stranger, and the One is seen in all. Today's word.
Your line: no stranger. Once today, look at the face of someone you'd normally walk past, a second time, and let them count. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-one.
